title: Bone is nearly as strong in tension as in compression

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bone is nearly as strong in tension as in compression

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Fresh bone resists tearing almost as well as it resists crushing (tensile strength about 9–12 and crushing strength about 13–16 kg per sq. mm), which makes it an economical structural material that can serve equally as tie or strut.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: At first sight, bone seems weak indeed; but it has the great and unusual advantage that it is very nearly as good for a tie as for a strut, nearly as strong to withstand rupture, or tearing asunder, as to resist crushing.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Mechanical properties of bone”. Scope: fresh (living) vertebrate bone

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim gives standard variables and numerical ranges, so contrary data would clearly refute it. Public records exist but are heterogeneous and do not adequately cover living vertebrate bone generally.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile matched tensile and compressive ultimate strengths of fresh bone by species, element and orientation, then test whether their ratio is near one and within the stated ranges.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Strength depends strongly on orientation, hydration, age and strain rate.

Fresh-bone paired tests are scattered.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.97
discriminating power: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical bands are a sharp decision rule. One open archive contains tensile curves for human femoral tissue and omits the matched crushing series Thompson quotes. A compilation of published material tests could finish the comparison for humans and a few other species, which is a real but partial test of fresh vertebrate bone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare ultimate tensile strength and compressive strength of fresh cortical bone, in kg per square mm, on matched specimens. The claim is confirmed if tension falls near 9-12, compression near 13-16, and the two are close; a large gap, or values far from those bands, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Dry, embalmed and demineralized specimens shift both strengths relative to fresh bone.

Open files emphasize tensile tests of elderly human femoral bone; paired crushing tests of fresh bone across vertebrates are scattered in papers.
